main_text.p: lim estis sequuti. Ita postea Ioramus rex, in Helisæum confert culpam famis, quæ Samariæ tanta erat, ut matres filios suos comederent. Rex furore correptus, mittebat seruum, qui prophetam interficeret, at præmonitus à Deo vitauit. Christianis eadem obiecta sunt, vt Tertullianus, Cyprianus, Arnobius & alij qui Apologias pro Christianis scripsere, testantur. Quoties enim Deus mundum afflixit, pruina, grandine, fame, peste, bello, aquarum inundatione, aut si qua alia calamitas publica incidisset, conclamatum est contra Christianos, Ad bestias, ad bestias, ad leones, tolle sacrilegos, scelestos istos homines non fas est viuere: indigni sunt, qui lucem aspiciant. Eusebius scribit histor. Eccles. libro nono, capite septimo, Imperatorem Maximinum passim edicta sua promulgasse, quibus indicauit, omnia mala, quæ mundus hactenus perpessus fit, propter purnitiosum istum errorem nefandorum illorum hominum, ( intelligens Christianos ) accidisse, qui vbique ferè terrarum

page.notes: Printed text is a fragment at the start (continues from previous page). Some words are doubtful in the scan: "purnitiosum" appears as printed (likely "pernitiosum", kept as printed). Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. The page ends mid-sentence at "terrarum", which continues on the next page. Text was reproduced with u/v and i/j normalised; the printed ligatures and spellings were kept.
